fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Capacity Metrics App - Health The Health page in the Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app is currently in Preview, and some minor updates/enhancements will be made to make it Generally Available. The page offers a high-level overview of all capacities for which a user is admin, aggregating capacity metrics across a tenant in a way that greatly simplifies the ability to identify capacities that are in need of attention. The page is designed to help capacity administrators quickly identify capacities that are consuming the most compute resources or are experiencing issues such as throttl

fabricroadmap.title: Capacity Metrics App - Timepoint Summary & Detail
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Capacity Metrics Metrics App - Timepoint Summary & Item Detail The Timepoint Summary and Item Detail pages in the Fabric Capacity Metrics app work together to give you a complete view of your metrics at any specific point in time.The Timepoint Summary page provides a 30-second snapshot of interactive and background operations ranked by compute impact, measured in Capacity Units (CUs). Visuals like the heartbeat chart show CU activity over a 60-minute window, making it easy to spot peaks and troughs. This experience centralizes the most critical controls and insights—such as around utilization, scaling, throttling, and surge protection—making it easier than ever to detect issues, manage resources, and remediate capacities quickly. Key initials features include CU utilization details with breakdowns (e.g., interactive/background

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound Access Protection for EventHouse
fabricroadmap.summary: Public Preview: Q2 2026

fabricroadmap.title: Govern Skills for Fabric
fabricroadmap.summary: Govern Skills bring AI-powered governance assistance to Microsoft Fabric, helping admins monitor their data estate, identify governance risks, and take recommended actions from a single experience. Built around the core governance pillars of Health, Protect, and Trust, the skills provide contextual insights and remediation guidance to help organizations maintain a well-governed, secure, and trusted data estate.

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound access protection for Mirrored DBs
fabricroadmap.summary: Outbound access protection is one of the top security asks from the Fabric Enterprise customers. Today WS OAP support only limited set of items which limits the adoption of Fabric for Customers. Our aim is to support Mirrored DBs in OAP so that customers can prevent sensitive data from getting exfiltrated.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric OneLake catalog in Excel Get Data
fabricroadmap.summary: The OneLake catalog integration in Excel as part of modern Get Data unlocks seamless connectivity to Fabric data, empowering every business user to discover and analyze organizational content directly from Excel. This powerful capability simplifies data access and accelerates insights, making Excel a true gateway to Fabric’s rich data ecosystem.

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound Access Protection for (RTI) Real Time Dashboards
fabricroadmap.summary: Public Preview: Q2 2026

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Capacity Overage
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric capacity overage is an opt-in feature in Microsoft Fabric that automatically bills for excess capacity usage in a pay-as-you-go basis instead of throttling operations - enabling capacity administrators to protect capacities from being throttled. Today, as a capcity admin, you can use surge protection, resize capacities, or pay for dedicated capacities to try to protect mission critical jobs, but all these approaches still can result in throttling and rejection due to insufficient provisioned capacity. Overage billing addresses this consideration. The solution allows a capacity admin to

fabricroadmap.title: Surge Protection V2 (Workspace-level)
fabricroadmap.summary: Workspace-level surge protection helps capacity administrators prevent a single workspace from unexpectedly consuming an entire capacity. Administrators can set workspace consumption limits, exempt mission-critical workspaces, and block or unblock workspaces to maintain capacity health and quality of service. There will also be an API that supports these actions alongside an API for the existing Capacity-level Surge Protection feature as part of this release. Finally, there will be the ability to opt-in to notifications via email - and see them in product - when a surge protection activity occ

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake Catalog - govern with centralized management capabilities (domains, tags, capacities, etc)
fabricroadmap.summary: The OneLake Catalog – Govern experience is expanding by introducing a comprehensive set of management tools designed to reduce fragmentation and simplify day-to-day administration. Enable admins to centrally govern the data they own from a single, unified place, supporting operations at scale while maintaining speed and agility. Deliver a consistent and intuitive admin experience across tenant, domain, capacity, and workspace scopes, ensuring governance is predictable and easy to apply regardless of where data resides. Provide flexible and granular governance controls that adapt to different o

fabricroadmap.title: Find Fabric items and tables from Copilot CLI with OneLake Catalog
fabricroadmap.summary: As part of Skills for Fabric, AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot can discover Fabric items and tables. Developers can find existing, governed data before writing code, enabling a "find before you build" workflow that bridges AI tools and Fabric's enterprise data platform.

fabricroadmap.title: Query item downstream and upstream relations through a public API
fabricroadmap.summary: Query upstream and downstream item relationships across all Fabric workloads through a public API. Retrieve which items depend on or feed into a given item, spanning Lakehouses, Warehouses, Pipelines, Semantic Models, Reports and more.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake catalog Search API expansion to OneLake and Semantic model tables
fabricroadmap.summary: The OneLake Catalog Search API (POST /v1/catalog/search) — previously limited to Fabric items — now also returns OneLake tables (e.g. Lakehouse, Mirrored) and Semantic Model tables as first-class search results. Items and tables are ranked together in a single, unified relevance-scored result set — so the most relevant result surfaces first regardless of entity type.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Chargeback app
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Chargeback app - Tags Support Chargeback app tagging will enable organizations to attribute and analyze capacity consumption across customer-defined business dimensions such as project, function, workspace, cost center, or department. This enhancement will provide greater flexibility for cost allocation, chargeback, and reporting scenarios, helping customers align Fabric consumption with their internal financial and organizational structures.About the app: The Microsoft Fabric Chargeback app helps customers understand which teams, users, and workloads are driving capacity usage, enablin

fabricroadmap.title: Capacity Metrics app
fabricroadmap.summary: The Capacity Metrics app will features a redesigned experience with modernized visualizations, improved navigation, and enhanced analytics capabilities that make it easier to monitor, understand, and optimize Microsoft Fabric capacity usage.The updated experience provides clearer insights into utilization trends, workload consumption patterns, and performance bottlenecks, helping administrators more quickly identify capacity constraints, investigate throttling events, and make data-driven decisions to improve capacity health and efficiency.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Materialized Lake Views - Multi Workspace/Lakehouse execution support
fabricroadmap.summary: Multi Lakehouse support in Lineage enables users to visualize and manage dependencies of Materialized Lake Views (MLVs) across multiple workspaces and lakehouses, providing a unified view that helps prevent data silos and improves transparency. It is designed to support scalable lineage tracking, advanced search, and focused navigation, making it easier for data teams to trace upstream and downstream dependencies.

fabricroadmap.title: Lakehouse Query Window
fabricroadmap.summary: On the data exploration front, the new Lakehouse Query Explorer introduces a streamlined, in-context query experience directly within the Lakehouse. Users can write and run Spark SQL queries right from the Lakehouse explorer to quickly discover and analyze data, with intelligent suggestions and real-time error prevention all without needing to navigate to a notebook. Results can be saved as Spark Views, visualized as charts, filtered, sorted, and downloaded, with rich contextual information throughout. When deeper analysis is required, code can be seamlessly promoted into a notebook for more c

fabricroadmap.title: Custom Live Pools
fabricroadmap.summary: Customers can create custom compute pools for Spark with libraries and other items specific to their scenario and keep them warm like they can today with starter pools.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Runtime 2.0 - Public Preview
fabricroadmap.summary: This a new Fabric Runtime 2.0 release based on Spark 4.x and Delta Lake 4.x. Most importantly, it will have Scala 2.13 and will be based on Mariner 3.0 OS.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Runtime 2.0 - General Availability
fabricroadmap.summary: This a new Fabric Runtime 2.0 release based on Spark 4.x and Delta Lake 4.x. Most importantly, it will have Scala 2.13 and will be based on Mariner 3.0 OS.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Release Channel - Public Preview
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature enables multiple runtime channels for customers. The default channel will remain the current standard runtime, while an EarlyAccess channel will provide the latest updates - such as library upgrades and security vulnerability fix..Using Spark settings in the environment, customers can test and validate these changes early, before they become part of the default runtime channel.

fabricroadmap.title: Display the job concurrency and queueing limits to users as part of workspace settings
fabricroadmap.summary: Visibility into Job Concurrency & QueueingWorkspace users and admins can see all active jobs and their states (running, queued, throttled)Diagnose job delays by identifying concurrency limits or queueing bottlenecksCapacity admins can now monitor job activity across all workspaces based on CU load.Understand overall load and capacity pressure

fabricroadmap.title: CSV Support for Native Execution Engine
fabricroadmap.summary: Enhance the Native Execution Engine in Microsoft Fabric Spark to support CSV ingestion natively, minimizing fallbacks to the Spark JVM and improving performance for data ingestion workflows.Unlock native engine speedups for foundational ingestion scenarios.Reduce cost and latency during ETL, especially for write-heavy delta loads for customers given majority of users have CSV based file dependencies

fabricroadmap.title: Materialized Lake Views Support Incremental Update & Delete Propagation via Unique Key
fabricroadmap.summary: Materialized Lake Views will soon support incremental handling of updates and deletes from source tables by defining a unique key column on the MLV itself. When rows are modified or removed in the source, all related data changes will be automatically propagated to the materialized view during the next refresh — eliminating the need for full recomputation.

fabricroadmap.title: Environment - Support for Python Notebook
fabricroadmap.summary: Python Notebooks now integrate with Environments, enabling users to upload and use custom libraries and packages.

fabricroadmap.title: CI/CD: notebook resources in git and deployment pipeline and support for API
fabricroadmap.summary: Modules and files stored in the Notebook Resource folder can now be committed to Git and published through Deployment Pipelines.

fabricroadmap.title: Trigger Based Scheduling for Materialized Lake Views
fabricroadmap.summary: FMLV will support trigger-based execution of Materialized Lake Views — complementing existing scheduled and ad-hoc runs — by integrating with the Fabric event mechanism to allow customers to automatically refresh MLVs in response to events such as onelake events, Fabric Job events

fabricroadmap.title: Support Column-Level quality checks in Materialized Lake views
fabricroadmap.summary: FMLV will introduce column-level data quality constraints within the MLV framework — inspired by the widely adopted Deequ library — enabling customers to define and enforce quality rules directly on their Materialized Lake Views, addressing strong demand for built-in column-level quality controls.

fabricroadmap.title: Declarative file data ingestion experience in Fabric Materialized Lake Views
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric data engineers today write 80-100+ lines of boilerplate PySpark to ingest CSV and Parquet files into Delta tables - handling file discovery, schema inference, incremental refresh, schema drift, and error recovery manually. This feature introduces a simple Spark SQL DDL surface (CREATE MATERIALIZED LAKE VIEW ... FROM OneLake_Files OPTIONS (...)) that declaratively handles all of this. It includes automatic schema evolution (or strict fixed-schema mode), three refresh modes (append_only, mirror, full), built-in error handling, structured user telemetry on files and lakehouse-level DAG lin

fabricroadmap.title: [Monitoring] Integrate and Expose Spark Application CPU/Memory Usage
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature is designed to visualize real-time metrics for Spark applications through a dashboard that allows users to monitor CPU and memory utilization at the application level for both executors and drivers, across running and completed applications. It aligns with the Fabric SaaS offering and extends Spark vCore allocation and utilization analysis. Additional details about user scenarios are available in the discussion.

fabricroadmap.title: [GA] Job Insights Library
fabricroadmap.summary: The general availability of the Job Insights Library provides comprehensive visibility into Spark execution by surfacing logs and metrics across queries, jobs, stages, and tasks. Users can not only analyze execution behavior directly within the experience but also download and store driver and executor logs to Lakehouse or other destinations, enabling persistent storage, deeper analysis, and integration with downstream monitoring workflows.

fabricroadmap.title: Spark Workspace Monitoring v1
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature delivers a comprehensive Spark Workspace Monitoring experience, enabling administrators and data engineers to gain full visibility into workspace-level Spark activity. Users can view and analyze live and historical job executions, filter and drill into specific runs, and compare performance across Fabric items.With direct access to Spark diagnostic logs and metrics via Kusto Query Language (KQL), users can create custom queries, perform advanced aggregations, and build their own dashboards, unlocking powerful, flexible insights for monitoring, troubleshooting, and optimization.

fabricroadmap.title: Track and Manage Notebook Run Dependencies & Linage View
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature delivers a comprehensive Notebook Run Lineage experience for Spark applications, enabling data engineers to monitor and analyze complex notebook workflows with ease. It provides an at-a-glance view of all notebook run statuses, helps quickly identify root-cause failures across nested executions, and highlights performance bottlenecks. Users can filter and explore large execution graphs, access detailed error and run-level information, and view aggregated summaries of execution health and resource usage—all in one place.

fabricroadmap.title: Spark Diagnostic Emitter for Spark 4.1
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature updates the Spark diagnostic emitter to support the upcoming Spark 4.1 release while maintaining full compatibility with existing capabilities, including Log Analytics (legacy and new APIs), Event Hub, and Blob Storage.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Runtime 1.3 Mariner 3.0 Upgrade
fabricroadmap.summary: We are upgrading the underlying operating system of Fabric Runtime 1.3 from Mariner 2.0 to Mariner 3.0, delivering improved security, performance, and long-term support for Apache Spark workloads. This upgrade brings the latest OS-level patches, enhanced container compatibility, and a modernized base image that aligns with the latest Azure infrastructure standards.To ensure a smooth transition, the upgrade leverages the Runtime Release Channel feature, which allows customers to preview and validate the Mariner 3.0-based runtime before it becomes the default. Data engineers can switch to the re

fabricroadmap.title: Synapse Release Channel - Public Preview
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature enables multiple runtime channels for customers. The default channel will remain the current standard runtime, while an EarlyAccess channel will provide the latest updates - such as library upgrades and security vulnerability fix..Using Spark configuration, customers can test and validate these changes early, before they become part of the default runtime channel.

fabricroadmap.title: Runtime 2.1 (Spark 4.2 and Delta 4.4)
fabricroadmap.summary: Microsoft Fabric Runtime 2.1 updates the Apache Spark foundation to Spark 4.2 and Delta Lake 4.4, with Python 3.14, Scala 2.13, and Java 21. For supported workloads, the Native Execution Engine is enabled by default to provide acceleration without extra configuration, while documented opt-out and controlled fallback paths preserve compatibility.Runtime 2.1 also introduces a leaner built-in package baseline with PySpark and SparkR. Customers can add compatible optional Python and R libraries through Library Manager or a Fabric Environment, reducing package conflicts while preserving flexibility

fabricroadmap.title: Connectors - Oracle connector with built-in driver
fabricroadmap.summary: Oracle connector in Data Factory now allow users to connector with built-in driver. Customer now can connect to Oracle system without installing driver through on-premise gateway.

fabricroadmap.title: Connectors - New connector in Copy Job and Pipeline activities
fabricroadmap.summary: New connectors are planned in Copy job, and Pipeline activities 1. Impala (as source)2. Jira (as source)3. Netezza (as source)3. Hive (as source)4. HubSpot (as source)5. Shopify (as source)6. Square (as source)7. Xero (as source)

fabricroadmap.title: Pipelines - Refresh Materialized Lake View Activity
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Materialized Lake Views are a revolutionary way to declaratively define views, built on data stored in your lakehouse that automatically materializes the results of the data transformation as a physical Delta table. Now we have a pipeline activity that you can automate and schedule to regularly refresh your MLV or add it to the end of your ETL pipeline.

fabricroadmap.title: Dataflows - New Destination: Google Cloud Storage
fabricroadmap.summary: We are introducing Google Cloud Storage (GCS) as a new data destination for Dataflow Gen2 in Preview, enabling customers to land transformed data from Microsoft Fabric directly into Google Cloud Storage using Dataflow Gen2’s low‑code Power Query experience.This preview expands Dataflow Gen2’s destination ecosystem to better support multi‑cloud data architectures, giving customers with existing investments in Google Cloud a simple way to integrate Fabric‑based transformations into their broader data estate.Key benefits and scenarios: Publish curated outputs from Dataflow Gen2 directly to Google

fabricroadmap.title: Connections - Enabling customers to parameterize their connections
fabricroadmap.summary: Data engineers encounter challenges when constructing metadata-driven workflows due to the need to establish multiple connections for diverse data source endpoints. Currently, existing connections lack the capability for dynamic referencing. To address this, we are introducing connections as a workspace item that will consolidate the connections Role Based Access Contro l(RBAC) with workspace. This feature will facilitate dynamic referencing in connections, thereby enhancing flexibility and efficiency in metadata-driven workflows.

fabricroadmap.title: Airflow - Workspace logs integration for Diagnostics
fabricroadmap.summary: We will enhance the Diagnostics experience for Apache Airflow jobs developers by surfacing logs in the Fabric Workspace Monitoring experience.

fabricroadmap.title: Dataflows - Output Destinations: Recents Support
fabricroadmap.summary: We plan to bring support for Recents to the Output Data experience, allowing users to easily reconnect to a recently used Output Destination, much like we have made available in the Get Data experience.

fabricroadmap.title: Dataflows - Dataflows Gen2 Partitioned Compute
fabricroadmap.summary: Partitioned Compute is a capability of Dataflow Gen2 that enables parts of a dataflow to run in parallel, reducing the time to finish its evaluations.Partitioned compute targets scenarios where the Dataflow engine can efficiently fold operations that can partition the data source and process each partition in parallel. For example, in a scenario where you're connecting to multiple files stored in an Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, you can partition the list of files from your source, efficiently retrieve the partitioned list of files using query folding, use the combine files experience, and pro

fabricroadmap.title: Dataflows - Support for Mapping Data Flow transformations in Dataflow Gen2
fabricroadmap.summary: Mapping Data Flow transformations are coming to Dataflow Gen2, bringing the proven, low‑code Spark-based transformation capabilities of Azure Data Factory and Azure Synapse directly into Microsoft Fabric. With this enhancement, customers can author and run complex data transformations at scale using the same visual, code‑free experience they rely on today—now natively integrated into the Fabric Dataflow Gen2 experience.This capability unlocks the full power of Mapping Data Flows within Fabric, enabling advanced transformations that are optimized for large datasets and predictable performance.

fabricroadmap.title: Dataflows - My Queries
fabricroadmap.summary: We plan to make My Queries in Dataflow Gen2 generally available, enabling users to save commonly used Power Query transformations to a personal library and reuse them across multiple dataflows.Moving My Queries to GA means it is ready for production usage, with the reliability, consistency, and support required for standardizing data preparation at scale.Key benefits and scenarios: Reuse proven transformation logic—such as cleansing steps, business rules, or standard joins—without rebuilding queries from scratch Promote consistency and reduce duplication when building multiple dataflows agains

fabricroadmap.title: Mirroring - Google BigQuery
fabricroadmap.summary: Mirroring for Google BigQuery enables customers to continuously replicate BigQuery data into Fabric OneLake, making it easier to use BigQuery data with Power BI, data engineering, data science, and AI experiences in Fabric. Customers can bring data from Google BigQuery into the Fabric analytics estate without maintaining separate ETL pipelines for common replication scenarios.

fabricroadmap.title: Connectors - Modernized Exchange connector for Power Query
fabricroadmap.summary: Microsoft Fabric will introduce a modernized replacement for the existing Exchange connector, improving the foundation for connecting to Exchange data through Power Query-based experiences.

fabricroadmap.title: Connectors - Improved Google BigQuery connector reliability and query support
fabricroadmap.summary: Microsoft Fabric will improve the Google BigQuery connector experience by addressing query folding, data type handling, and connector reliability issues, enabling more consistent data access and transformation scenarios through Power Query-based experiences.

fabricroadmap.title: Dataflows - New Destination: PostgreSQL
fabricroadmap.summary: We are introducing PostgreSQL as a new data destination for Dataflow Gen2, enabling customers to publish transformed data from Microsoft Fabric directly into PostgreSQL databases using Dataflow Gen2’s low‑code Power Query experience.This release expands Dataflow Gen2’s destination ecosystem to better support operational, analytical, and application integration scenarios, giving customers a simple and flexible way to operationalize Fabric‑based data transformations in PostgreSQL environments.Key benefits and scenarios: Publish curated outputs from Dataflow Gen2 directly into PostgreSQL database

fabricroadmap.title: Airflow - Workspace Identity Support
fabricroadmap.summary: Apache Airflow jobs in Fabric provide the most effective and easy way to build DAG workflows using our built-in Python code editor. Now that we have enabled workpsace identity (WI) support for our Fabric providers, orchestrating Fabric jobs from Airflow is super easy.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - Copy data from/to Fabric Event Stream
fabricroadmap.summary: Customers will be able to work with real‑time data by using Copy jobs to move data from Fabric Event Streams to supported destinations, or to copy data from supported sources into Fabric Event Streams as a destination.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - Auto-partitioning on large tables with Oracle, SAP Hana and Lakehouse table
fabricroadmap.summary: Copy Job Auto‑partitioning automatically splits large tables into parallel partitions when copying data from Oracle, SAP HANA, and Lakehouse tables, improving throughput, scalability, and overall copy performance for large‑scale ingestions.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - Extended SCD Type 2 support to Fabric Warehouse and Synapse SQL
fabricroadmap.summary: Copy Job – Extended SCD Type 2 support enables automated historical data tracking when copying data to Fabric Warehouse, and Synapse SQL, preserving full change history for downstream analytics and auditing use cases.

fabricroadmap.title: Dataflows - Performance: Disable V-Order Compression
fabricroadmap.summary: The option to disable V‑Order (VertiParquet) compression in Dataflow Gen2 will become generally available, giving customers greater control over performance and storage optimization trade‑offs for supported workloads and destinations.This capability enables advanced users to reduce processing overhead associated with V‑Order compression during writes, helping improve refresh throughput and lower write latency for large-scale or time-sensitive ingestion and transformation scenarios.With this release, organizations can better tune Dataflow Gen2 execution behavior to align with the performance re

fabricroadmap.title: Airflow - Dataflow Gen2 Refresh
fabricroadmap.summary: With Microsoft Fabric Apache Airflow Job, you can easily orchestrate your Fabric processes. Now with a built-in Microsoft provider to run Dataflow refreshes from your Airlfow DAG, you can easliy leverage Dataflows from your DAG.

fabricroadmap.title: Dataflows - New Data Destination: AWS S3
fabricroadmap.summary: We are introducing Amazon S3 as a new data destination for Dataflow Gen2 in Preview, enabling customers to publish transformed data from Microsoft Fabric directly into Amazon S3 using Dataflow Gen2’s low‑code Power Query experience.This preview expands Dataflow Gen2’s destination ecosystem to better support multi‑cloud data architectures, making it easier for customers with existing AWS investments to integrate Fabric‑based transformations into their broader data lake and analytics environments.Key benefits and scenarios: Publish curated outputs from Dataflow Gen2 directly to Amazon S3 buckets

fabricroadmap.title: Gateways - Performance improvement in VNet gateway through the modern .NetCore evaluator enablement
fabricroadmap.summary: We are introducing a .NET (NetCore) query evaluator for the VNET data gateway.The evaluator executes mashup queries; moving it to a modern .NET runtime modernizes how queries run. With this update:- Query evaluation on the VNET data gateway runs on a modern .NET runtime.- Performance, security, and long-term supportability improve.- The gateway is positioned to benefit from ongoing .NET investments.This reliability and performance investment is available initially as a preview.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - AI-powered Error Assistant and Insight for Copy Job
fabricroadmap.summary: Copilot helps to troubleshoot Copy job error messages by providing clearer summary and actionable recommendations.

fabricroadmap.title: Dataflows - Performance: Disable V-Order Compression
fabricroadmap.summary: Dataflow Gen2 will introduce a new preview capability that allows customers to disable V‑Order (VertiParquet) compression for supported workloads and destinations, giving advanced users greater control over execution behavior, performance characteristics, and cost trade‑offs.This capability is especially valuable for scenarios where write latency and refresh throughput are prioritized over downstream storage optimization. By disabling V‑Order compression, customers can reduce processing overhead during writes, helping accelerate refresh performance for large or time‑sensitive ingestion and tra

fabricroadmap.title: Pipelines - Support added for schedule parameters
fabricroadmap.summary: Hyper-parametrization in Data Factory pipelines enables powerful reusable generic patterns and is very popular in Data Factory. Now with parameter support in schedules you can create schedules that have specific parameter values to create complex execution patterns.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - SAP with ABAP add-on
fabricroadmap.summary: Copy job for SAP with ABAP add-on enables organizations to bring SAP data into Microsoft Fabric using a Microsoft Data Integration ABAP Add-On installed on the SAP server. It extends Fabric’s built-in SAP connectors and supports copying tables, views, and CDS views from supported SAP systems with both full and incremental copy modes.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - CDC based replication to Oracle
fabricroadmap.summary: Customers can use Copy job to automatically capture inserts, updates, and deletions from any supported CDC source store, and replicate them to the new destination stores including Oracle without requiring a watermark column.

fabricroadmap.title: Pipelines - Support pipeline parameters in schedules
fabricroadmap.summary: Pipelines in Fabric Data Factory emphasize general re-use patterns and metadata driven methodologies. Now with support for pipeline parameters in schedules you can create multiple schedules per pipeline with different parameter values enabling incredibly powerful generic pipeline workflow patterns.

fabricroadmap.title: Pipelines - Set the "Run As" identity of the pipeline from the pipeline schedule
fabricroadmap.summary: When automating your Fabric Data Factory pipelines, you will greatly benefit from having the flexibility to set the identity (i.e. user, SPN, workspace identity) of the pipeine at the time of execution. With this feature, you can now set it easily from the scheduler API and scheduler UI.

fabricroadmap.title: Airflow - Workspace Monitoring to include Apache Airflow logs from Airflow Job
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Apache Airflow jobs provides a SaaS way to build Python-based Airflow DAGs in your Fabric workspace. With this new feature, you will now be able to easily view your runtime logs from Apache Airflow in the Fabric Workspace Monitoring view to build your own queries, reports, and dashboards.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - Auto-enable CDF on Delta table creation from Copy job
fabricroadmap.summary: Change Data Feed can be automatically enabled for Delta tables created by Copy job, allowing downstream workloads to directly leverage the Delta Change Data Feed to track all data changes.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - Activator support for triggering Copy jobs
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Activator can trigger Copy job executions in a native way, allowing event‑driven scenarios without pipeline where a file landing in storage automatically initiates a Copy job.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - CDC based replication from Salesforce
fabricroadmap.summary: Copy job provides a Salesforce CDC connector, allowing you to capture row‑level inserts, updates, and deletes from Salesforce and replicate them to any supported destination.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - CDC based replication from PostgreSQL
fabricroadmap.summary: With the PostgreSQL CDC connector in Copy job, you can capture inserts, updates, and deletes from PostgreSQL and copy them to any supported destination.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - CDC based replication from MySQL
fabricroadmap.summary: With the MySQL CDC connector in Copy job, you can capture inserts, updates, and deletes from MySQL and copy them to any supported destination.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job - Support composite watermark columns for incremental copy
fabricroadmap.summary: Incremental copy from Copy job will support composite watermark columns for complex change detection, including scenarios where the maximum watermark is derived from multiple incremental columns such as LastCreateDateTime and LastModifiedDateTime together.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy Job/Activity - Improve read performance for Parquet format when source is a single large file
fabricroadmap.summary: Improve the read performance when reading a single large parquet file in Copy job and Pipeline activities (Copy activity, Lookup activity, GetMetadata activity, Delete activity) by allowing multi-threads.

fabricroadmap.title: Gateways - Autoscaling gateway clusters for VNet Gateway
fabricroadmap.summary: For VNet data gateways, the fixed node setup can be inefficient during high-demand periods. To improve this, we're introducing auto-scaling, which dynamically adjusts the number of nodes based on demand.

fabricroadmap.title: Connections - Enhanced Connection Collaboration Model
fabricroadmap.summary: To enhance security, we aim to prevent the sharing of Microsoft account credentials across collaborators. The new connection-sharing model will encourage each collaborator to sign in with their own Microsoft account.

fabricroadmap.title: Connectors - Oracle Connector support without requiring a gateway
fabricroadmap.summary: Oracle connector supports cloud-based scenario by bundling the Oracle Data Provider NET driver and avoiding users having to use an On-premises data gateway for Cloud-only scenarios.

fabricroadmap.title: Copy job -  Change Data Capture (CDC) capability GA with SQL estates
fabricroadmap.summary: The Change Data Capture (CDC) capability in Copy Job is generally available with Azure SQL DB, SQL Server and SQL MI

fabricroadmap.title: Pipelines - Run Pipeline when dependencies are met
fabricroadmap.summary: A commonly used functionality in ADF is configuring a Pipeline to run when a set of dependencies are met. We are excited to bring this functionality to Data Pipelines in Data Factory in Fabric to continue enriching orchestration capabilities.

fabricroadmap.title: Dataflows - New Destination: Google BigQuery

Customers continue to benefit from the familiar, guided Migration Assistant experience as they modernize their data warehouses to Fabric.

fabricroadmap.title: Migrate to Fabric DW using SQL files
fabricroadmap.summary: Migrate to Fabric Data Warehouse enables customers to upload a compressed (zip) of .sql files to initiate the migration. The new approach simplifies and accelerates the early stages of migration while reducing manual preparation and risk. Customers continue to benefit from the familiar, guided Migration Assistant experience as they modernize their data warehouses to Fabric.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Web: Streamlined Git and Deployment Pipeline Support with DacFx
fabricroadmap.summary: DacFx onboarding in the Fabric Web editor enables seamless Git integration and supports deployment pipelines for Fabric Warehouse. With DacFx, developers can reliably manage schema changes, version control database projects, and execute incremental, non-destructive deployments directly from the web editor. This integration ensures that changes are tracked, deployments are safe, and pipelines can be automated, aligning with best practices for CI/CD in enterprise data environments.

fabricroadmap.title: Browse and Connectivity in VS Code for Fabric Warehouse
fabricroadmap.summary: VS Code allows developers to explore Fabric Workspaces and connect directly to Fabric Warehouses, providing seamless access to data and objects. Key capabilities include: Workspace exploration: Navigate Fabric Workspaces, including their warehouses, tables, views, and other artifacts. Direct connectivity: Connect to one or multiple Fabric Warehouses from VS Code for querying or management. Integrated workflow: Quickly access schemas and objects for development, debugging, or CI/CD without switching tools.

fabricroadmap.title: Organize multitasking tabs in groups
fabricroadmap.summary: Stay focused when working across many open items by grouping tabs. Create named groups, organize related work, and collapse or expand them as needed.

fabricroadmap.title: Allow users to reorder open workspaces in the nav bar
fabricroadmap.summary: Currently, users can open multiple workspaces simultaneously and switch between them via the navigation bar. However, the order of these workspace icons is fixed based on the sequence in which they were opened.This creates friction for users who frequently multitask across workspaces and want to organize their open items in a way that better reflects their workflow priorities.This feature allows users to reorder open workspace icons in the navigation bar through drag-and-drop interaction, enabling greater control and efficiency in multitasking.

fabricroadmap.title: Associate an identity with Fabric items and schedules
fabricroadmap.summary: Microsoft Fabric items and their schedules today implicitly execute under user identities (owner or creator), which makes production workloads fragile: pipelines, schedules, copy jobs, and shortcuts break when owners leave the organization or their tokens expire, and existing takeover flows only shift the dependency to another user rather than removing it. With this release, Fabric introduces associated Identity: a durable, user-selected execution identity that can be attached to an item through new UI and APIs, starting with Workspace Identity support and Schedule Run-as. fabricroadmap.summary: The Fabric Extensibility Toolkit (FET) now provides migration support from the Workload Development Kit (WDK), enabling developers to transition existing workloads to the modern FET platform with minimal friction. This capability ensures continuity for solutions built on WDK while unlocking advanced features. Migration guidance includes documentation, and best practices to streamline the process — from updating manifest versions to adopting new APIs and SDKs.

fabricroadmap.summary: Expands right-click support across key Fabric surfaces, enabling users to quickly open content in a new browser tab without navigating away.

fabricroadmap.title: Git Integration - Allow contributor and above users to switch branch
fabricroadmap.summary: Today, when a Fabric workspace is connected to a Git repository, only workspace admins can switch the selected branch. With this change, Contributor and above users can also switch branches. Additionally, Contributor and above users will be able to branch out to existing workspaces that have this setting enabled, even if they aren't admins on the target workspace. This new capability will be available via Fabric UI and Fabric REST API.

fabricroadmap.title: Git Integration - Branched Workspaces
fabricroadmap.summary: Branched workspaces introduce a redesigned developer experience for branch-out operations. Visual cues now show which workspaces are related, making it easier to navigate feature branches. New capabilities streamline the branch-out workflow and give developers more control over their feature workspaces.

fabricroadmap.title: Git Integration - Selective Branching
fabricroadmap.summary: When developers branch out to work on a specific feature, they can now select only the items they need instead of copying all workspace items to the target. This reduces setup time and lets developers start coding faster.

fabricroadmap.title: Git integration - compare code changes
fabricroadmap.summary: When developers want to sync their workspace with the git repo, they want to view the changes made before taking actions.With this feature we will enable viewing the exact changes since the last sync between the workspace and the branch, as well as where those changes are.It will be shown as code compare experience that is familiar to developers. Devs can see what items and files have been changed, see the exact code changes and whether it is in a Fabric workspace, or in the repo.

fabricroadmap.title: Bulk import and export item definition API
fabricroadmap.summary: Import and export item definitions in bulk through a single API call. Enables workspace-as-code workflows, simplifies CI/CD pipelines, and accelerates cross-workspace migrations by eliminating the need to handle items one at a time.

fabricroadmap.title: Git Integration - Branch workspace admin profile
fabricroadmap.summary: Branch workspace admin profile (aka. admin delegation) lets developers use the branch-out experience without needing create-workspace or assign-capacity permissions. Workspace admins keep full control through pre-configured guardrails while unblocking developer workflows. Capabilities: - Developers without create-workspace or assign-capacity permissions can perform branch-out seamlessly - Admins pre-configure profile to ensure guardrails for branch workspaces: developer role, capacity assignment and admin list.

fabricroadmap.title: Git Integration - File level commit
fabricroadmap.summary: Commit individual files within a supported Fabric item to Git, rather than committing the entire item at once. File-level commits give developers granular change history, support partial commits of in-progress work, and produce smaller, easier-to-review pull requests.

fabricroadmap.title: Multiple task flows in a workspace
fabricroadmap.summary: The multiple task flows in a workspace feature enables users to create, manage, and navigate multiple independent task flows within the same workspace. Each task flow has its own isolated canvas, clear identity, and lifecycle, allowing teams to organize work by project or process without impacting others.

fabricroadmap.title: Enable/disable Fabric multitasking context carry across browser tabs
fabricroadmap.summary: We’re improving Fabric’s multitasking experience by giving users control over how context behaves when they open Fabric in another browser tab. Today, open items, tab order, pinned items, and tab groups automatically carry over to additional tabs in the same browser profile. fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Core MCP Server (GA)
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Core MCP Server is a secure, cloud-hosted MCP endpoint that lets AI agents perform authenticated operations in Microsoft Fabric. It exposes Fabric public APIs as typed MCP tools for catalog search, workspace and item management, permissions, folders, capacity discovery, and long-running operations. Requests authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID, respect Fabric RBAC, and are recorded in Fabric audit logs. General availability removes the need for customers to install or operate a local server for these workflows.

fabricroadmap.title: Salesforce zero-copy integration with OneLake
fabricroadmap.summary: Salesforce integration with OneLake allow users to query, visualize and build AI agents on data stored in Salesforce and OneLake without moving, copying or complex ETL pipelines.

fabricroadmap.title: ServiceNow zero-copy integration
fabricroadmap.summary: ServiceNow Workflow Data Hub adds a zero-copy connector to Microsoft OneLake. Workflow Data Fabric is an enhanced data integration layer that unifies business and technology data across the enterprise, powering all workflows and AI agents with real-time, secure access to data from any source. With this integration, customers can access tables in OneLake using the Table APIs powered by Apache Iceberg.

fabricroadmap.title: Intuigence AI
fabricroadmap.summary: Synthetic AI engineers for Industrial Operations that help users automate routine tasks so human engineers can bring their ingenuity to creative and complex challenges.Its industrial semantics, ontologies, physics aware models and purpose built agents supply the understanding that turns raw data into industrial grade operational intelligence using RTI on Fabric as the backbone. Eventstreams capture and transform data at massive scale, eventhouse delivers fast and flexible analytics and OneLake ensures that context is unified and discoverable.

fabricroadmap.title: Scaled Configuration Canvas

The scaled design features unified navigation, scalable and expandable elements, and better interaction patterns for clearer entities, relationships, rules, and more. fabricroadmap.title: Public query API for Ontology
fabricroadmap.summary: The public query API for Microsoft Fabric IQ Ontology gives developers programmatic access to supported ontology query capabilities. Applications and automation can query ontology-backed data using the supported query interface rather than requiring users to run every query interactively. This release concerns the query API; management of ontology definitions and the client management SDK are tracked as separate capabilities.

fabricroadmap.title: [Ontology for Copilot Studio] Ontology integration with CoPilot Studio
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric IQ Ontology serves as a first-class context source within Microsoft Copilot Studio, enabling you to build custom agents that understand your business domain out of the box. By connecting your ontology to Copilot Studio, your custom agents gain access to a structured semantic layer that defines your entity types, relationships, and business concepts — allowing them to reason over real operational data and deliver domain-aware responses without requiring custom prompt engineering or manual data wiring.

fabricroadmap.title: Ontology Versioning
fabricroadmap.summary: Change your Ontology with confidence. Every saved version is listed newest-first with its timestamp, author, and description, so teams building an Ontology together can always see what changed, who changed it, and roll back to any earlier state.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Planning
fabricroadmap.summary: Planning in Microsoft Fabric is a native enterprise planning capability that brings budgeting, forecasting, and scenario modeling directly into your data platform—eliminating silos between planning, analytics, and AI.Built into Microsoft Fabric, Planning enables business and data teams to collaboratively create, manage, and refine plans on top of governed, real-time data—powering faster, more informed decision-making across the organization.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph delivers reliable performance at billion scale
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph is designed to operate at very large scale, supporting graphs with billions of elements while maintaining predictable performance and reliability. Ongoing investments improve query stability, ingestion throughput, and service resiliency. Operational visibility is enhanced by exposing detailed ingestion failure information and clearer diagnostic signals, enabling customers to identify, understand, and resolve issues more quickly as graph workloads scale into production.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph enables fast insight with no/low code graph modelling, querying and exploration
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph provides low code and no code experiences for modelling graphs, building queries, and exploring results. Customers can define graph models, manage reusable queries, and inspect outputs through UI driven workflows without requiring deep GQL expertise. These experiences lower the barrier to entry for analysts and application builders, while still allowing advanced users to drop down to full GQL for complex scenarios.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph makes connected data accessible through natural language data agents
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph integrates with Fabric Data Agent and supports NL2GQL, enabling users to ask questions about graph data in natural language. Queries are translated into GQL, executed against the graph, and returned as grounded results. Users can inspect the executed query or navigate back to the graph experience for deeper exploration. This capability allows Fabric Graph to participate directly in agent driven and Copilot scenarios while maintaining transparency and trust.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph expands GQL support for real world relationship queries
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph increases GQL feature coverage to support richer relationship modeling and investigation scenarios. This includes dynamic nested data, OPTIONAL MATCH, extended FOR semantics (IS SOURCE OF, IS DESTINATION OF, COLLECT ONE), result shaping functions (NODES, EDGES, INNER NODES), quantified simple edge patterns, and shortest path queries.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph enforces OneLake security for governed graph access
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph conforms to OneLake security so that access controls defined over lake data are enforced consistently when data is represented and queried as a graph. Row , column , and object level policies apply end to end, preventing graphs from becoming an alternate access path. This alignment ensures customers can adopt Fabric Graph without introducing new security models or weakening existing governance and compliance controls.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph supports private network access for enterprise environments
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph supports private connectivity using Fabric private endpoints and private links. This allows customers to access graph workloads over private networks, keep traffic off the public internet, and deploy Fabric Graph in locked down enterprise network environments. The service validates graph APIs under private access configurations and propagates the required access context for trusted service to service communication.

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound Access Protection for Fabric Graph
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric Graph complies with Fabric Workspace Outbound Access Protection (OAP). When OAP is enabled, graph workloads enforce outbound network policies, allowing connections only to approved destinations such as managed private endpoints. Non compliant outbound calls are blocked and surfaced clearly. This ensures Fabric Graph aligns with enterprise network security requirements and helps prevent unintended or unauthorized data exfiltration.

fabricroadmap.title: Ontology item GA
fabricroadmap.summary: General availability of the Microsoft Fabric IQ Ontology item enables teams to maintain a shared model of business entities, properties, and relationships in Fabric. Modelers can connect those definitions to supported data sources and provide business context to supported analytics and agent experiences. The release covers the ontology item and its supported capabilities; individual integrations, security features, and advanced modeling capabilities retain their own release milestones.

fabricroadmap.summary: Resource Links let you attach resources to the entity types they describe, so insights live alongside the data model that powers them. Starting with Power BI reports, when someone explores an entity in your ontology, they can immediately see the relevant Power BI reports that show how that data is analyzed, monitored, and used without needing to search across tools or guess which report applies.

fabricroadmap.title: [Ontology for Foundry IQ] - Ontology integration with Foundry IQ
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric IQ Ontology integrates with Azure AI Foundry to provide data scientists and AI builders with rich semantic context for training, grounding, and fine-tuning models and agents. By connecting ontology-defined business concepts, entity relationships, and domain vocabulary to your AI workflows, Foundry IQ enables more reliable agent behavior, improved reasoning over business processes, and better alignment between AI outputs and the real-world structure of your enterprise.

fabricroadmap.title: [Ontology for A365] - Ontology integration with Agent 365
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric IQ Ontology integrates natively with Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent 365, providing AI agents with a rich semantic source of truth for reasoning over your business data. When users ask questions in natural language, agents leverage the ontology to understand the relationships between business entities, interpret intent consistently, and deliver grounded, accurate answers drawn directly from your enterprise data — all within the familiar Microsoft 365 experience.

fabricroadmap.title: [Ontology for Data Agent] - Ontology integration with Data Agent
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric IQ Ontology empowers the Data Agent to query and reason over your business data using natural language, grounded in a well-defined semantic model. Users can ask complex analytical questions and receive trustworthy, explainable answers with citations that trace back to the underlying ontology and data sources — giving teams confidence that insights are accurate, verifiable, and rooted in the true structure of their enterprise data.

fabricroadmap.title: Modeling Untyped Properties
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature allows users to create property definitions without immediately selecting a data type or binding to a data source. Users can define high‑level business concepts first and assign data types later when real data is bound, at which point the entity type updates automatically. This flexibility lets users model concepts early without needing to know data types or source details upfront.

fabricroadmap.title: [Ontology MCP Endpoint] Query Tools
fabricroadmap.summary: The Ontology MCP Endpoint provides a programmatic query surface that enables any AI agent or application to discover, explore, and reason over ontology data. Query tools support natural language search over ontology data, schema discovery through entity type and property listing, and structured entity/relationship traversal — giving developers and agents a single, consistent API to ask questions, retrieve answers, and build intelligent experiences grounded in your enterprise semantic layer.

fabricroadmap.title: [Ontology for Operational Agent] - Ontology integration with Operations Agent
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric IQ Ontology enables operational agents to reason over your live business environment using natural language, providing frontline teams with explainable, trustworthy answers backed by citations. Operational agents use the ontology as their semantic backbone to interpret questions about asset status, process state, and operational relationships — delivering grounded insights that help operators make faster, better-informed decisions without needing to navigate multiple data systems.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric Graph integration with Ontology: From shared business meaning to connected-data insights
fabricroadmap.summary: Fabric IQ brings Ontology and Graph together so customers can move from a shared business model to advanced relationship analysis. Customers can understand how business concepts connect, choose the data most relevant to their scenario, and use Graph for multi-step impact analysis, dependency exploration, and path-based questions.

Users receive onboarding and migration guidance so they can understand the transition and its effect on their ontology workflows. Supported guidance should be reviewed before migration; this release does not promise that every connected experience migrates without additional steps.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake malware scanning
fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake malware protection helps secure your data by automatically scanning files for malicious content when they’re uploaded. It surfaces alerts and scan results for further action, providing built‑in protection for enterprise data without requiring additional infrastructure.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake catalog - tables data preview and quick actions
fabricroadmap.summary: With this new feature, OneLake catalog can display user-defined descriptions for tables and columns, helping users quickly understand data context. Once a table is identified as relevant, users can instantly preview its data with a single click - streamlining discovery and accelerating informed decision-making. This enhancement fosters trust, promotes collaboration, and encourages a culture of data reuse across the organization.

With these capabilities, users can simplify complex schema management in file data processing and gain complete control using Shortcut Transformations. You can preview and align schemas, automatically handle column mapping, and ensure data types remain consistent. The ingestion process is optimized for speed and reliability. With this update, you can transition from familiar Excel workflows to modern lakehouse architecture effortlessly, making analytics faster and collaboration easier.

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcut Transformations - Customize ingestion with user configurations
fabricroadmap.summary: With the upcoming enhancements to Shortcut Transformations, you’ll be able to fully customize how you bring in data from CSV, Parquet, JSON, and Excel files. You can set file encoding, choose custom quote or escape characters for your data in case of CSV files. For CSV, Parquet and JSON files, you’ll have options to decide refresh mode (Append Only or Mirror) and schema mode (Dynamic or Fixed). All these controls will be available directly in the user interface, giving you more flexibility, reliability, and efficiency in managing your data ingestion and transformation workflows.

fabricroadmap.title: Shortcut Transformations - Enhanced monitoring experience
fabricroadmap.summary: With the latest improvements to Shortcut Transformations, you’ll have a much more transparent and actionable monitoring experience. fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake provides rule-based lifecycle management to help organizations optimize storage costs. These policies allow administrators to automatically transition data between hot, cool, and cold tiers based on last access or modification time.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake Storage Lifecycle Management Policies
fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake provides rule-based lifecycle management to help organizations optimize storage costs. These policies allow administrators to automatically transition data between hot, cool, and cold tiers based on last access or modification time.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake security - ReadWrite permission - GA
fabricroadmap.summary: Configure write permissions for folders in a lakehouse using OneLake security. With this feature, viewers can be given selective write access to certain folders in the lakehouse enabling teams to write data without having Contributor or higher roles in the workspace.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake security - dynamic and multi-table RLS
fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake security is adding support for dynamic and multi-table row level security. With dynamic RLS, users can create roles in OneLake that secure data differently for each user that queries the data. In addition, multi-table RLS allows data to be secured by querying values in a lookup table. Combined, these features empower users to complex RLS rules for securing enterprise data.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake security granular APIs
fabricroadmap.summary: In addition to the existing bulk API for managing OneLake security roles, we will add a new set of APIs for performing granular actions against roles.Examples include: create a single role, add a single member to a role, etc.

fabricroadmap.title: Data Quality: Persist and Inspect Corrupt Rows in Shortcut Transformations
fabricroadmap.summary: Shortcut Transformations today silently drops corrupt rows during file-to-Delta ingestion - users see a count of rejected rows in telemetry but have no way to inspect what failed, which file it came from, or when it was rejected. It's estimated that 35% of all jobs encounter corrupt rows that are silently discarded. This feature persists corrupt rows alongside valid data in the destination Delta table with source file path and ingestion timestamp, enabling direct inspection via SQL/Power BI, downstream remediation in silver-layer pipelines, and compliance audit trails. fabricroadmap.title: OneLake file explorer GA
fabricroadmap.summary: OneLake file explorer will offer the full support that comes with Generally Availablity (GA). The OneLake file explorer application seamlessly integrates OneLake with Windows File Explorer. This application automatically syncs all OneLake items that you have access to in Windows File Explorer."Sync" refers to pulling up-to-date metadata on files and folders, and sending changes made locally to the OneLake service. fabricroadmap.title: Outbound access protection for Power BI (Semantic Models)
fabricroadmap.summary: Workspace admins responsible for safeguarding organizational data will be able to leverage Outbound Access Control (OAP) in Fabric to ensure that Semantic Models and Power BI Reports are permitted to connect only to explicitly approved data sources. OAP helps to prevent data exfiltration by blocking data connections to unapproved or potentially risky endpoints, thereby enforcing organizational data governance and compliance requirements.

fabricroadmap.title: Power BI relative slicers week starts on option
fabricroadmap.summary: Specify when your week starts for relative date options for weeks.

fabricroadmap.title: Power BI Vega visual
fabricroadmap.summary: Customize the presentation of your data in a Power BI report with a Vega specification.

fabricroadmap.title: Power BI Markdown visual
fabricroadmap.summary: Display Markdown in your Power BI report from your data or entered manually.

fabricroadmap.title: Filter action button to show filter options on the visual
fabricroadmap.summary: Bringing the filter pane to your visual with a new top level action buttons in your visual title.

fabricroadmap.title: Sort action button to show filter options on the visual
fabricroadmap.summary: Bringing the sort options to your visual with a new top level action buttons in your visual title.

fabricroadmap.title: Azure Maps geocoding auditor
fabricroadmap.summary: Show information about how Azure Maps converted your location to the map, called geocoding, when you are editing your Power BI report.

fabricroadmap.title: Azure Maps multiple data layers
fabricroadmap.summary: Add different data for each layer of your Power BI Azure Maps visual.

fabricroadmap.title: Table and matrix fixed width columns
fabricroadmap.summary: A new option in the Table and Matrix visuals to specify each columns width.

fabricroadmap.title: Matrix expand and collapse icons on column headers
fabricroadmap.summary: Adding expand and collapse icons to the column headers when more than one column is added, like how there are expand and collapse icons for row headers when there are more than one row added to the matrix in Power BI.

fabricroadmap.title: Donut Chart - Center Value
fabricroadmap.summary: Display a total, custom measure, or label directly in the center of donut charts, eliminating the need for overlaying a separate card visual. The center value responds to filters, selections, and scales automatically across all platforms.

fabricroadmap.title: Card Visual - Trend Chart
fabricroadmap.summary: Display a built-in trend chart (line or column) inside Card visuals to show how values change over time. No SVGs or extra visuals needed.

fabricroadmap.title: Visuals categorical axis "scroll starts from" option (scroll from right)
fabricroadmap.summary: Formatting pane options for where the scroll bar starts from when visible on the axis of a visual. For example, if I have a line chart showing trends over time, I can set this to scroll from right and when viewers open the report the latest data points show first and they can scroll to the left to see the historical trend.

fabricroadmap.title: OneLake file URLs for report visuals
fabricroadmap.summary: Reference OneLake files directly in your report visuals for images and maps.

fabricroadmap.title: Design ribbon in Power BI Desktop
fabricroadmap.summary: Design ribbon for quick access to build-in themes, page size, page background, wallpaper, and links to the theme gallery and how to create a custom theme for your Power BI reports.

fabricroadmap.title: Explore
fabricroadmap.summary: Explore data in a focused experience without creating a report. Quickly investigate and customize your analysis using matrices and visuals, then save the exploration to a workspace or as a report.

fabricroadmap.title: Date picker slicer to set relative and manual date ranges
fabricroadmap.summary: Adds a date picker mode for date slicers so authors can pick a relative default range (e.g., “last full month”) that automatically rolls forward as time passes when published, without authors having to update the report each period. Report viewers can override it to filter to other relative ranges or any manual date range.

fabricroadmap.title: Quick visual edits
fabricroadmap.summary: Previously known as On-object interaction, Quick visual edits makes it easier to build and format visuals directly from the report canvas. Add or remove data, manage visual elements, and update common settings such as titles, subtitles, legends, and data labels in context. For advanced customization, continue in the Format pane.

fabricroadmap.title: Modern visual defaults and customizing theme improvements
fabricroadmap.summary: New visual defaults to overhaul the Power BI base report theme to create professional looking reports in seconds. This update incorporates many of the latest updates we have made to reports and report theming. This update also includes increasing the default page size to 1080x1920. Report theme customizaton improvements such as color palettes and custom theme authoring from the formatting pane available in both Desktop and web.

fabricroadmap.title: Date picker slicer to set relative and manual date ranges

Report viewers can override it to filter to other relative ranges or any manual date range.

fabricroadmap.summary: We are bringing TMDL View in the web

fabricroadmap.title: DirectQuery support for editing semantic models in the Power BI service
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature brings DirectQuery (DQ) support to Power BI web modeling, enabling users to create and edit DirectQuery and Dual models directly in the browser. Today, DirectQuery authoring is only available in Power BI Desktop.

fabricroadmap.title: Visual calculations GA
fabricroadmap.summary: A visual calculation is a DAX calculation that's defined and executed directly on a visual. Visual calculations make it easier to create calculations previously hard to create, right in the visual.

fabricroadmap.title: Org Apps GA
fabricroadmap.summary: Org Apps allows you to easily create different apps for different pruposes with full source control support. In this upcomming release we will close alot of the most requested features and take Org Apps to General Availability.

fabricroadmap.title: Narrative Visual Support in PaaS embed
fabricroadmap.summary: This new capability will support the Narrative Visual in PaaS report embedding

fabricroadmap.title: Developer Mode GA
fabricroadmap.summary: We will be GAing developer mode in Desktop which will include the new PBIR format being default on for everyone. More details to follow.

fabricroadmap.title: DAX User Defined Functions
fabricroadmap.summary: User-Defined Functions (UDFs) allow you to encapsulate reusable, parameterized DAX logic into named functions that can be called across measures, calculated columns, and visual calculations throughout your semantic model. UDFs support both value and expression parameters, enabling you to centralize complex business logic—like tax calculations or currency conversions—so it's written once and maintained in a single place. Functions can be created in DAX Query View or TMDL View and appear as first-class objects under a dedicated "Functions" node in Model Explorer

fabricroadmap.title: Enhanced Report Consumption Copilot with Fabric IQ
fabricroadmap.summary: Powered by Fabric IQ, this enhancement to Report Consumption Copilot improves answer quality by delivering more accurate and relevant responses to data questions, helping users better understand and explore report content through natural language.

fabricroadmap.title: Audience support in Org Apps
fabricroadmap.summary: This improvement to Power BI's Org Apps will add support for defining user access and content display by audience(s), like the functionality in Power BI workspace apps. Audiences will allow for conditional display of content in the org app according to the audience or audiences a user belongs to. For instance, app creators can create one audience that can see only a subset of report within the app, but another audience with managerial oversite to make use of all of the reporting.

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound access protection for Power BI (Reports)

fabricroadmap.title: Set as landing page in Power BI reports
fabricroadmap.summary: Always make sure your report viewers land on the right page

fabricroadmap.title: Tooltip options for Power BI visuals

fabricroadmap.title: Shape map visual in Power BI reports

fabricroadmap.title: Input slicer numeric support
fabricroadmap.summary: Input slicer to allow numeric data colors for filtering and forced numeric entry.

fabricroadmap.title: Conditional formatting for lines and series/labels in Power BI visuals
fabricroadmap.summary: Conditional formatting to be available for series in Power BI visuals. This includes lines, markers, and legends.

fabricroadmap.title: List slicer with dropdown mode
fabricroadmap.summary: List slicer with drop down mode and advanced search options.

fabricroadmap.title: Gantt chart visual
fabricroadmap.summary: A new core visual in Power BI -- the gantt chart, visualizing all your product tasks in a Power BI report.

fabricroadmap.title: Add to preset for Power BI visuals
fabricroadmap.summary: Take the formatting on an individual visual and add it to the custom report theme for re-use on other visuals in the same report or a new report.

fabricroadmap.title: Organizational themes for Power BI reports
fabricroadmap.summary: Organizational themes (preview) allow Power BI administrators to centrally manage and distribute custom report themes across the organization. Maintaining a consistent visual identity across Power BI reports is now simpler and more scalable, thanks to organizational themes. Whether reports are built manually or generated with Copilot, this feature ensures that styling and branding stay aligned with your organization's identity and design standards.

fabricroadmap.title: Report Ribbon in the web
fabricroadmap.summary: The new Report Ribbon on the web brings the familiar Power BI Desktop ribbon experience to the browser, providing a more intuitive, organized, and consistent way to access report actions and authoring capabilities.

fabricroadmap.title: Developer mode (PBIP) external changes reload
fabricroadmap.summary: External Changes Reload enables Power BI Desktop to automatically detect and apply changes made to PBIP project files by external tools such as Visual Studio Code, without requiring users to restart Power BI Desktop.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream reference data join with one lake delta tables
fabricroadmap.summary: The Reference Data Join feature in Eventstream enables you to enrich streaming events by joining them with static or slowly changing delta tables in one lake.User can reference any one lake delta tables using lakehouse, and join it with streaming data in eventstream to enahace and add additional context to their events during processing.

fabricroadmap.title: Azure Service Bus source connector for Eventstream
fabricroadmap.summary: Eventstream now provides a generally available Azure Service Bus source connector. Customers can bring messages from Service Bus queues and topics into Microsoft Fabric for real-time processing without custom code.With this capability, you can:- Connect Eventstream to Azure Service Bus queues and topics.- Route Service Bus data to Fabric destinations for analysis and alerts.

fabricroadmap.title: Real-Time hub left-navigation consolidation for Data Sources
fabricroadmap.summary: To improve clarity and task completion in Real Time hub, we’re streamlining the left navigation. Users have reported confusion due to multiple overlapping entry points, making it difficult to locate the right actions for their real-time data workflows. By consolidating and simplifying the left-navigation menu, we aim to reduce cognitive load and help users quickly identify the most relevant entry point for their tasks.

fabricroadmap.title: Eventstream supports customers to upload own connector
fabricroadmap.summary: This feature enables customers to develop or reuse their own Kafka connectors, or open-source Kafka connectors, when no pre-built streaming connector is available.With this capability, you can:- Customize your own connector at your own pace.- Run with no infrastructure to manage.- Reuse open-source connectors directly.

fabricroadmap.title: Lakehouse Streaming Tables in the Real Time hub
fabricroadmap.summary: Lakehouse Streaming Tables bring real-time data processing and analytics to the Fabric Real Time hub, making it easier for data engineers and data scientists to discover, explore, and act on streaming data - all in one central location. With seamless integration to Spark and AI Skills, users can filter, open, and endorse streaming tables, and launch advanced analytics experiences. This feature is designed to boost engagement and productivity by providing instant access to continuously updated data, supporting rapid insights and decision-making for modern data teams.

fabricroadmap.title: Outbound access protection for Azure and Fabric Events
fabricroadmap.summary: Outbound Access Protection (OAP) in Microsoft Fabric restricts outbound connectivity from a workspace to external destinations unless explicitly allowed by administrators, helping prevent data exfiltration and enforce security policies.

fabricroadmap.title: Fabric IQ ontology as operations agent source
fabricroadmap.summary: Operations agents will be able to use the semantic information in the Fabric IQ ontology as a knowledge source, monitoring the entities and data and taking actions accordingly.

fabricroadmap.title: Better feedback on OA playbook problems
fabricroadmap.summary: When you give operations agents instructions and create its rules and playbook, it gives feedback when properties couldn't be grounded with data actions couldn't be grounded rule conditions were detected that are unsupported couldn't detect any rule/condition duplicate Id columns detectedThis helps you tailor your goals and instructions so the agent learns how you want it to operate.

fabricroadmap.title: Analyze Business Events in Eventhouse
fabricroadmap.summary: Route and analyze Fabric Business Events in Eventhouse for real-time querying and analytics.

fabricroadmap.title: Secure Fabric Eventstreams with customer-managed keys
fabricroadmap.summary: Apply Fabric workspace customer managed keys to Eventstreams to add an extra layer of encryption for data at rest. When CMK is enabled for a workspace, Eventstreams automatically use the workspace key configuration via Azure Key Vault, including key rotation and revocation handling.

fabricroadmap.title: Variable Library support for Eventstream
fabricroadmap.summary: Eventstream now integrates with the Fabric Variable Library, so configurations can reference workspace variables. This makes Eventstream definitions portable across development, test, and production workspaces.With this capability, you can:- Reference workspace variables for connection identifiers and item references.- Reuse a single Eventstream definition across environments by swapping variable values.- Manage configuration centrally in the variable library instead of editing each item.

fabricroadmap.title: Enable stream processing and real-time analytics on Mirror DB change feeds
fabricroadmap.summary: Mirror DB integration with Real-Time Intelligence in Microsoft Fabric lets organizations track and process updates to their Mirrored data sources like Azure SQL, Mirroed Snowflake and others. By enabling change feeds on these mirrored datasets, users can quickly build event-driven and AI-powered applications—like dashboards and alerts—without complex setup or deep knowlege of Apache Spark. This streamlined approach delivers instant insights and automation, helping businesses respond to evolving data in real time.

fabricroadmap.title: Unify batch & streaming data platforms with CopyJob & Real-Time Intelligence
fabricroadmap.summary: The integration of Real-Time Intelligence with CopyJob in Microsoft Fabric empowers organizations to stream incremental updates from traditionally “batch” data sources directly into Eventstreams. Simultaneously, users can ingest data from streaming sources into any CopyJob destination that supports incremental updates. This unified experience makes it easy to build hybrid data platforms that combine batch and streaming assets.
